# [ci] fix: clean up orphaned vLLM processes after Ascend E2E tests

[Upstream PR](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8337) · state: closed · merged: True

## Original PR description

### What does this PR do?

Stop Ray and kill remaining VLLM processes after both GSM8K and GEO3K runs, including on failure, to release NPU resources for subsequent tests. Log NPU status after cleanup.

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Continue vLLM cleanup if Ray stop fails.**

If `ray stop --force` exits nonzero, the fail-fast shell ends the cleanup step. Neither `pkill` nor `npu-smi info` then runs. An orphaned vLLM process can retain NPU resources after a failed run. Capture the Ray stop result in both cleanup steps, run the remaining commands, and report the failure afterward. GitHub Actions uses fail-fast shell behavior for `run:` steps. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax))

As per retrieved learnings, GitHub Actions `run:` steps use `set -e` by default.






Also applies to: 134-134

@wucong25 `always()` makes the cleanup step run after a prior failure. It does not prevent the shell from exiting when `ray stop --force` fails.



- Update both cleanup steps in `.github/workflows/e2e_ppo_trainer_veomni_vllm_ascend.yml`.
- Capture the Ray exit status without stopping cleanup.
- Run `pkill`, wait five seconds, and run `npu-smi info`.
- Report failures after cleanup completes. Continue to treat `pkill` exit status `1` as “no matching processes.”
